title: SLO Sanity Canary and Capacity Validation Harness
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview:
This document defines the SLO Sanity Canary and Capacity Validation Harness — an operational playbook and executable checklist teams use to validate that SLOs, error budget policies, and capacity provisioning behave as expected before, during, and after changes (deployments, model onboardings, scaling events). The harness is intended for both scheduled experiments and gated pre-production canaries that run against production-like traffic.

Purpose and goals:
- Validate that SLO telemetry and alerting pipelines correctly surface degradation within the expected time window.
- Confirm error budget burn calculations and automated throttles/eviction behave within policy.
- Exercise capacity backfills, soft preemption, and graceful degradation paths without impacting customer-visible SLOs beyond tolerance.
- Provide a reproducible checklist for runbook authors and oncall engineers to run controlled canaries and capture evidence for post-exercise review.

Scope:
- Applies to model-serving clusters, request-routing and admission control components, and the capacity orchestration layer (autoscaler/ejection controller).
- Not a replacement for large-scale chaos campaigns; this is a targeted, low-risk verification harness suitable for frequent use.

Who should use this document:
- Service owners, SREs responsible for the tenant/model, release engineers, and product engineers onboarding new workloads.

Ownership and schedule:
- Primary owner: SRE serving-runtime team
- Secondary owner: Service stewardship (product/infra leads)
- Recommended cadence: run as part of major model rollouts, quarterly for high-traffic tenants, and after infra autoscaler or admission-control changes.

Prerequisites and environment:
1) A canary environment or a production shadowing configuration with the ability to route 0.1%–5% of production traffic to the canary.
2) Canary must have separate telemetry tags (canary=true) and token-level sampling enabled for evidence capture.
3) Access to the SLO dashboard, error budget ledger, capacity planner, and incident escalation channels.
4) Ability to run controlled synthetic load via the test harness (see example below).

Telemetry signals and thresholds (table):
- Signal: p99 latency (model_inference_ms) | SLO threshold: <= 1200 ms | Canary acceptance: p99 <= 1100 ms
- Signal: requests_with_errors / total_requests (user-visible errors) | SLO threshold: <= 0.5% | Canary acceptance: <= 0.4%
- Signal: token_cost_per_1k | Budget impact threshold: 10% increase allowed for trial | Canary acceptance: <= 5% change
- Signal: kv_cache_hit_ratio | Soft-fallback threshold: >= 70% | Canary acceptance: >= 75%
- Signal: autoscaler_scale_events_per_min | Abuse threshold: < 3/min | Canary acceptance: <= 1/min

Canary scenarios (runbook):
1) Baseline sanity check (no injected stress)
   - Objective: ensure telemetry ingest, SLO calculation, alerting and dashboards reflect the canary service correctly.
   - Steps:
     a) Deploy canary artifact into target pool with version tag canary/v1.
     b) Route 0.1% of traffic with token tag canary_token and start sampling.
     c) Verify p50/p90/p99, error rate, and token-cost metrics show stable values for 15 minutes.
     d) Confirm that alerts are not firing and error budget ledger shows +0 burn.

2) Regression simulation (synthetic tail latency)
   - Objective: exercise tail-latency paths and confirm SLO alerting and remediation signals appear in 5–10 minutes.
   - Steps:
     a) Increase request size for 5% of canary traffic: synthetic_client --qps 30 --frac-tail 0.05 --payload-size 8KB
     b) Observe p99 and p995 latency.
     c) Expect SLO alert to trigger when p99 > 1200ms sustained for 3m.
     d) Validate automated mitigation: route is demoted to low-priority lane and error budget burn is applied.

3) Capacity starvation (gradual overload)
   - Objective: validate autoscaler/ejection controller and graceful degradation behavior.
   - Steps:
     a) Inject sustained 2x traffic for 10 minutes: loadrunner --target canary_service --qps 2x-production --duration 10m
     b) Expect autoscaler to provision additional pods/GPUs within configured cooldown (8–15m).
     c) If autoscaler cannot provision, expect soft preemption: best-effort tenants are shed, and priority lanes preserved.
     d) Verify that SLOs for gold-tier tenants remain within tolerance; record evicted tenant IDs.

4) Error budget policy enforcement (fast burn)
   - Objective: confirm policy-based throttles and error-budget-driven fallbacks engage correctly.
   - Steps:
     a) Simulate a fast burn: synthetic_client --qps 500 --payload 2KB --error-injection 0.15 --duration 3m
     b) Observe error budget ledger: burn_rate should exceed configured critical threshold in 2–4 minutes.
     c) Expect automated throttle to reduce admission rate for non-critical tokens and trigger owner-notifications.
     d) Verify rollback: the controller reduces traffic for affected tenants and optionally falls back to cheaper model variant.

Acceptance criteria and decision matrix:
- Green: no SLO alerts and observed metric deltas within canary acceptance thresholds. Proceed to rollout.
- Yellow: transient alerts fired but automated mitigations corrected state within 10–20 minutes and error budget consumption < 20%. Proceed with caution and monitoring.
- Red: persistent SLO alerts, error budget consumption > 20% or any customer-visible degradation for > 30 minutes. Abort rollout and follow escalation procedure.

Runbook — step-by-step execution (numbered):
1) Pre-checks (owner + SRE):
   - Confirm run owner and oncall assigned.
   - Ensure rollback artifact and routing plan prepared.
   - Snapshot current error budget ledger and telemetry dashboards (time-stamped).
2) Deploy canary and start traffic routing at 0.1%
3) Run Baseline sanity check for 15 minutes and capture evidence (logs, traces, snapshots)
4) Execute scenario sequence (Regression -> Capacity -> Fast burn). Wait for steady-state validation between steps: 10 min for regression, 20 min for capacity, 5–10 min after fast burn.
5) After each scenario, record: metrics snapshot, oncall observations, automated mitigation events, and tenant impact summary.
6) Post-harness review: open a short review doc with evidence, lessons learned, and any remediations required.

Escalation and rollback procedures:
- If the experiment hits Red criteria: immediately revert traffic routing to pre-canary state and redeploy last-known-good revision.
- Notify SRE pager, product steward, and incident commander. Use channel #sre-critical and follow incident templates.
- If automated rollback fails, initiate oncall manual throttling: cli admissionctl set-rate --service canary_service --rate 0.01

Evidence collection and artifact checklist:
- Metrics snapshots (prometheus/Grafana links) with time ranges
- Traces for 10 representative failing requests (link or trace IDs)
- Error budget ledger export CSV
- Autoscaler logs and scale event timeline
- Load generator configuration and logs

Post-exercise review template (to be filled within 48 hours):
- Summary: brief description of test and outcome
- Observed anomalies: list and severity
- Root-cause hypothesis (if any)
- Actions and owners: remediation, instrumentation, policy changes
- Go/no-go recommendation for rollout

Implementation snippets and examples:
- Example autoscaler policy (YAML):
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: CanaryAutoscaler
  metadata:
    name: example-canary-autoscaler
  spec:
    targetService: canary_service
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 40
    scaleWindow: 10m
    coolDown: 8m
    priorityPreserve: ["gold-tier"]

- Example admission test command (shell):
  # route 0.1% production traffic to canary
  redwoodctl routing set --service canary_service --percent 0.1 --tag canary=true

- Example load runner command (JSON CLI):
  {"target": "https://canary.internal.redwood.ai/infer", "qps": "auto", "duration": "10m", "mix": [{"path": "/v1/generate", "weight": 1}], "special": {"tailFraction": 0.05}}

Operational tooling and automation ideas (suggested improvements):
- Integrate the harness with the SLO evidence pipeline so snapshots are stored automatically in the evidence store.
- Provide a single-button "Run Canary Harness" in the console that wires up routing, load generation, and evidence collection.
- Add canary-specific synthetic trace labels to make postmortem triage faster.

Safety and risk controls:
- Canary experiments must not exceed 5% of production traffic without explicit approval from SRE leads.
- All runs must include a prepared rollback artifact and a documented release owner.
- For high-sensitivity customers (PCI/PHI), only run synthetic-only canaries (no real customer traffic).

Appendix — quick checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Assign owner and oncall
- [ ] Prepare rollback artifact
- [ ] Configure canary routing (0.1% -> 1%)
- [ ] Enable token-level sampling and evidence collection
- [ ] Baseline sanity snapshot captured
- [ ] Run regression, capacity, fast-burn scenarios
- [ ] Capture evidence and open post-exercise review

For questions or onboarding help, ping #sre-canary-support and assign an owner in the harness run template.
